findings.title: escalation-ladder relaunch swallows the new exit 18, so a refused step is charged as an infra failure instead of the named operator hand-off (runners/orchid-drive:1088 `drive_launch ... || true` — the one of four call sites with no 18 arm; the task then burns infra_failures to `blocked` with no journal line and no operator-handoff boundary)

`drive_capability_refusal`'s once-per-record journal dedup compares against the run's persisted boundary, which `set_boundary` may never record (priority hold, or a second refused task winning the pass), so the same refusal line is appended every pass in exactly the case the comment says it guards
